blocks.content: Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript
Up to now, most of your interactivity has been simple:
Click a button → toggle a class → the UI changes.
That works perfectly when there are only two states, like:
But not every interface works with just two possibilities.
Imagine a section that displays multiple project cards. You do not want to show all of them at once. You want to show one card at a time and let the user move forward or backward through them.

blocks.alt: State is memory that drives behavior

blocks.content: How does the page know which card is currently visible? A simple toggle is not enough anymore. The page needs to remember something.
Next, you'll understand what a state is and how it helps control what the user sees.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
